text:
The measured UGBW (24.7 MHz vs. 43 MHz) and slow settling point to too little input-pair transconductance, while gain, phase margin, polarity, and power look right. Power implies a 30 µA tail, so the 3.02× mirror ratio (M5/M6) and the tail current are probably intact. The small offset (−2.2 mV) argues against a mismatch in the matched pair, so the fault is most likely a sizing change in the input device M1, with M2 and M5 as the next candidates. This is a ranking from circuit reasoning, not a simulation sweep.

```json
{"ranking": ["M1", "M2", "M5"], "fault": "Input-pair NMOS M1 sized wrong (W/L altered from the design value, likely L too long or W too small), reducing gm1 below the ~5.4e-4 S needed for 43 MHz UGBW at 2 pF; the other specs remain met."}
```
